_doc: Weekends and holidays (Week.weekend_menu): once per free day, at home before noon, Aunt Haruka asks how you'll spend it. Each activity costs hours (minutes), gives its effect, and picks one line. {who} = the person you're closest to.
ask: Aunt Haruka is wiping the counter. "No school! What's the plan, Toru? Don't say 'sleep'. Okay, you can say 'sleep'."
"A free day!" Aunt Haruka hands you a mochi for breakfast. "Help me in the shop, or go and be seventeen somewhere. Your choice."
Kiku is sitting on the counter swinging her legs. Aunt Haruka can't see her. "Day off," Haruka says. "How are you spending it?" Kiku mouths: 'shop'.
Rain on the shutters. "Even on a wet day off you shouldn't mope," says Aunt Haruka. "What'll it be?"

lines: You wrap mochi until your fingers smell of rice flour. A tourist couple asks if the shop is haunted. Kiku waves at them. They buy three boxes.
Aunt Haruka teaches you to shape cat mochi. Yours look like potatoes with ears. They sell first.
Old Tomi-san from the school store comes in and tells you your grandfather once let her pay later for a whole winter. She pays you back with gossip.
A first-year in a black hood buys one mochi, very slowly, and doesn't look at you once. He comes back four times.

activities.t: Go fishing at the harbour with Gen-san.
lines: Gen-san catches nothing and talks the whole time about the night he saw Umibozu rise out of a storm. He puts a bowl of ramen on the breakwater 'for the sea' before you leave.
You catch a mackerel. Gen-san catches an old boot with a fish in it. You agree to call it a draw.
Fog on the harbour. A voice from a boat that isn't there asks to borrow a ladle. Gen-san hands over one with no bottom, without looking up. "Funayurei. Polite ones," he says.
Herons on the breakwater. Gen-san says the Shirasagi family used to own every boat in the harbour. "Now they own the harbour and no boats," he says, and spits.
The library is empty except for a stone statue of a boy carrying firewood, reading. You're almost sure it wasn't there yesterday.
You actually learn something. You also find a 1901 town record with the name 'Asagiri Soichiro' crossed out in red.
Reiji is at the next table with a pile of files. Neither of you speaks for two hours. It's oddly comfortable.
You fall asleep on a history book and dream of rain on a hill. Still, you studied. Mostly.
You and {who} walk the whole length of the town and back, talking about nothing. It's the best kind of day.
{who} drags you to the arcade by the station. You lose every game. {who} wins a cat keyring and gives it to you.
You spend the afternoon at the river with {who}, skipping stones. The kappa skips one back.
{who} shows you a place in Suzunari you've never been: a tiny overgrown garden behind the shops with a single, perfect hydrangea.
You sleep until noon. The pillow is turned round when you wake up. Somebody small has left a sweet on it.
You sleep through two of Hayate's calls and four of Amane's messages. The fourth one is just a cat sticker.
You dream of nothing at all for the first time in weeks. You wake up starving and happy.
